metaDescription: Order custom medals for corporate awards, events, and recognition programs. Bulk pricing available. Shop now at Perfect Imprints.
introHtml:
Custom medals are typically made from durable zinc alloy or brass with a polished or antique finish, giving them a substantial feel that recipients appreciate. Many feature a ribbon attachment and can be customized with full-color enamel or laser engraving for detailed logos, text, or year markings. The weight and thickness of the medal — often measured in inches or millimeters — directly affect the perceived quality, so bulk buyers should consider options like die-struck or die-cast construction for crisp detail on large orders.

Whether you are a marketing director planning a company sales contest, an HR director organizing a service anniversary program, or a safety manager rewarding injury-free milestones, custom medals provide a tangible symbol of achievement that employees and partners value. They work equally well for trade show giveaways, fundraising event medals, and conference attendee recognition. With a range of ribbon colors and attachment styles available, these awards can be tailored to match your brand colors and event theme.
buyingGuideHtml:
When ordering custom medals, the first consideration is the construction method. Die-cast medals offer the sharpest detail for complex logos and are ideal for high-end awards. Die-struck medals are more economical for larger runs while still providing good definition. The finish — polished, satin, or antique — affects both appearance and durability. Antique finishes hide scratches better over time, making them a practical choice for medals that will be handled frequently.

Materials & Build Quality

Most promotional medals use zinc alloy or brass, with a protective coating to prevent tarnishing. The ribbon quality matters too: grosgrain ribbons are standard, but you can upgrade to satin or custom-printed ribbons that include your event name. The attachment ring should be sturdy enough to withstand repeated wear. For bulk orders, request a sample to verify weight and finish before committing to the full run.

Common Use Cases

Marketing directors use branded medals for customer loyalty programs and sales incentive contests. HR directors order personalized medals for employee service awards, safety milestones, and wellness program completions. Business owners often give logo medals at grand openings or community events. Safety managers find that bulk medals work well for recognizing accident-free days or safety training completions. Fundraising events and school programs also rely on wholesale medals as participation awards.

Decoration Options

Full-color enamel is the most popular decoration method for custom medals, allowing detailed logos and text. Laser engraving provides a sleek, permanent mark on metal without color, ideal for minimalist designs. For large quantities, screen printing onto the ribbon adds another branding opportunity. Some suppliers offer sublimation for full-color ribbon printing, which is especially effective for event-specific artwork.

Quantity Guidance

Minimum order quantities for custom medals typically start at 50 pieces, with the best per-unit pricing at 250 or more. Die-struck medals are cost-effective for runs of 100-500, while die-cast is better suited for smaller, premium batches. If you need multiple design variations (different place colors or event years), consider grouping them into a single production run to save on setup fees. Always factor in lead time: most custom medal orders take 2-4 weeks from artwork approval.

Common Buying Mistakes

One frequent error is choosing a finish that doesn't match the event tone — for example, a glossy finish for a formal awards ceremony can look cheap. Another is underestimating ribbon length: standard 24-inch ribbons fit most adults, but children's events may need shorter lengths. Also, avoid overly complex artwork on small medals (under 1.5 inches), as fine details may blur. Finally, confirm the attachment type — some medals use a pin back instead of a ribbon, which changes how they are worn.

faqs.q: What is the minimum order quantity for custom medals?
faqs.a: Minimum order quantities typically start at 50 pieces, though some suppliers offer lower minimums for stock designs. For full customization with your logo, plan for at least 100 units to get the best per-unit pricing.

faqs.q: What decoration methods are available for medals?
faqs.a: Common decoration methods include full-color enamel (soft or hard), laser engraving, and screen printing. Enamel provides vibrant colors and is durable, while laser engraving offers a sleek, permanent mark without color.

faqs.q: How long does production take for custom medals?
faqs.a: Production typically takes 2 to 4 weeks from artwork approval. Rush orders may be available for an additional fee. Always factor in shipping time when planning your event.

faqs.q: Can I get a sample before placing a bulk order?
faqs.a: Yes, most suppliers offer samples. Request a sample to verify the medal weight, finish, and ribbon quality. Some may charge a fee, but it is often refunded with a large order.

faqs.q: What sizes are available for custom medals?
faqs.a: Common sizes range from 1.5 inches to 3 inches in diameter. Smaller medals are suitable for participation awards, while larger sizes (2.5 inches or more) work well for top prizes. Thickness also varies, typically 1/8 to 1/4 inch.
